classification.difficultyReason: Represent given sine and cosine coordinates by drawing a radius at the stated angle of inclination.

content.prompt: Identify these points on the unit circle, showing the radius and angle of inclination. The first question has been done for you.

spec.description: Permanent completed demonstration with a unit circle, arrowed axes, radius at 70 degrees, coordinate label and highlighted angle sector.
spec.mathematics: The point is the endpoint of the unit radius inclined 70 degrees counterclockwise from the positive horizontal axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied demonstration visible in every edition.

answer.short: Radius at $25^\circ$ in quadrant I; endpoint labelled $(\cos25^\circ,\sin25^\circ)$.
answer.worked: Draw a unit circle with coordinate axes. Measure $25^\circ$ counterclockwise from the positive horizontal axis, draw the radius and label its endpoint $(\cos25^\circ,\sin25^\circ)$.

spec.description: Unit circle with radius and counterclockwise 25-degree sector; endpoint coordinate label above the figure with a leader.
spec.mathematics: The endpoint lies in quadrant I at inclination 25 degrees.

spec.description: Unit circle with radius in quadrant II and a counterclockwise 130-degree sector.
